notes: The Thinning Skeptic detail is the only position section carrying an external scientific rebuttal inside its own body ('more than 100 fire scientists... have pushed back hard on Hanson's methods'). It is paired with the skeptics' in-voice response, so it doesn't strawman — but for symmetry consider either noting that the Landscape Restorer evidence base is equally contested (by Hanson/DellaSala et al.) in that section, or letting the contest live only in the questions, as it does for every other pairing.

Action-kind asymmetry: the Thinning Skeptic's sole action is a 'donate' link (John Muir Project) while every other position gets a learn/policy/local link. A donate CTA reads either as stronger promotion or as 'this camp is only an advocacy shop' depending on the reader — consider a learn_more (e.g., FUSEE or the Ecosphere study) for parity.

Pre-colonial burn figure differs between sections: Basics stat says '~4.5M acres/yr' while the Cultural Fire Steward steelman says '4.4 to 12 million acres.' Both are defensible from the literature, but aligning on one attributed range avoids the appearance of lowballing the stat and highballing the steelman.

Crux subtitle 'two say the fire is a given and only the doorstep is ours' slightly flattens the Thinning Skeptic, who (via Ingalsbee/FUSEE) also backs prescribed fire, cultural burning, and managed wildfire — i.e., they would change the fire too, just not by backcountry thinning. A small rephrase ('only the doorstep is worth buying') would keep the four/two contrast without misdescribing them.

Question details occasionally adjudicate in the editorial voice — Q2's 'None of these is wrong' and Q6's 'most credible positions accept some version of both.' These describe genuine shared ground rather than pick a winner, so they don't breach neutrality, but attributing them ('all camps accept...') would be cleaner than asserting them.

The Jan-2025 LA firestorm Basics detail names Built-Edge Reformers and Suppression Modernizers as the camps who claim it as their strongest case; Climate-First Advocates also lean on that event (the WWA attribution cited in their own section). Adding them to that sentence would complete the triangulation.

No separate steelman for the timber-industry / regulatory-streamlining camp (the 'cut litigation, log more' case behind Fix Our Forests, e.g., AFRC and House sponsors) — its policy vehicle appears in why_now and, critically framed, inside the Thinning Skeptic section, while its nearest steelman is the science-flavored Landscape Restorer. This is within parity for a strong published topic since the fuels-side case is robustly carried, but an editor may want to decide deliberately whether it is a variant or a missing voice.

Thinning Skeptic deep detail: 'They don't claim the science is settled — more than 100 fire scientists... have pushed back hard on Hanson's methods' reads slightly outside the proponent's voice (Hanson does claim his findings are robust). The passage recovers by giving the skeptics' own reading of the pushback, so it is not a softening — but rephrasing from their perspective ('the pushback comes from the same establishment whose budgets his findings threaten, and he has answered it point by point') would be more fully in-voice.

Crux subtitle 'two say the fire is a given and only the doorstep is ours' compresses the Thinning Skeptic a bit hard — the FUSEE/Ingalsbee wing actively wants MORE fire on the land (prescribed, cultural, managed remote burns), not just doorstep defense. The compression is defensible for the megafire claim it summarizes, but a proponent might bristle at reading as pure fatalism.

Minor internal inconsistency: the beneficial-fire basics stat anchors pre-colonial California burning at '~4.5M acres/yr' while the Cultural Fire Steward section cites the full 4.4-12M acre estimate. Both trace to the same Stephens et al. range; labeling the basics figure explicitly as the low-end estimate would prevent a sharp reader seeing a contradiction.

Built-Edge Reformer's representative is a program (IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home) while the other five positions have named people or named institutions with a human anchor; Kimiko Barrett or Jack Cohen would match the pattern if a human face is preferred. Not a defect — the note explains the choice well.

Positive verification: the two freshest steelman-embedded claims both check out — FireSat's first three operational satellites launched July 7, 2026 (Muon Space/Earth Fire Alliance announcements), and the 62-72% severity-reduction figure matches the 2024 Tamm review meta-analysis (Davis et al., Forest Ecology and Management), correctly attributed to thin-plus-burn rather than thinning alone.

LA firestorm stat: the headline figures (16,251 structures destroyed, 31 deaths) are the CAL FIRE/AP one-year tallies and are accurate (AP's retrospective uses 16,246; tallies vary by a few structures), but the sole cited source (Moody's) itself says 'over 18,000 structures destroyed or damaged' and 'as many as 32 fatalities officially reported'. The $25-30B insured-loss figure does match Moody's exactly. Consider adding CAL FIRE/AP as a co-source or aligning the note's numbers with the cited page.

Initial-attack stat detail: the 98% national and 98.9% Pacific Northwest 2025 figures are confirmed on the USFS accomplishments page, but I could not directly confirm the 'best in 12 years' phrasing; soften or source it if it can't be pinned to a USFS statement.

Beneficial-fire scale stat anchors pre-colonial California burning at ~4.5M acres/yr, the low end of the Stephens et al. (2007) 4.4-11.8M acre range; the Cultural Fire Steward description correctly gives the full range. Labeling the basics figure as a low-end estimate would be extra-careful.

Karuk SB 310 agreement: the first-in-state agreement is confirmed, but the state task force describes it as signed in February 2025 while the draft says March 7, 2025 (the Karuk Tribe's announcement date); double-check the exact date against the tribe's press release.

Berkeley 17% defensible-space stat cites the Berkeley News article; the primary paper is 'Fire risk to structures in California's Wildland-Urban Interface', Nature Communications (2025), https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-63386-2 — worth citing directly at deep level.
IBHS premium-discount range in the Built-Edge description is '5-20%'; current reporting most often says 10-20% (varying by carrier and applying to the catastrophe-fire portion for Mercury). Minor.

Three source URLs (PNAS, Wiley/Ecosphere, Royal Society) return 403 to scripted requests but are publisher bot-blocks, not dead links — all three DOIs resolve to the correct papers (Abatzoglou & Williams 2016; Haugo et al. 2019; Westerling 2016).

The subtitle's four-vs-two mapping ('four camps would change the fire... two say the fire is a given') slightly flattens the Thinning Skeptic, who also backs good fire and emissions cuts; their distinctive claim (weather, not backcountry fuel, decides the destructive fires) does support the framing, but 'two say the destructive fires are decided by weather, and only the doorstep is ours' would be more precisely endorsable by Hanson or DellaSala.

In the subtitle, 'in the sky' is presumably the Climate-First camp (the atmosphere), but a reader may map it to Suppression Modernizer aircraft and then find only three of the 'four camps' accounted for — consider a phrase that unambiguously points at climate, e.g. 'in the atmosphere'.

The empirical crux line is dense (two long clauses joined by a semicolon); splitting the treatment-effectiveness question from the attribution-ledger question would scan better in the atlas register, though distribution may handle this.

Above-fold coverage is genuinely self-sufficient: all six positions have a compact evidence anchor above the fold (fire deficit → Landscape Restorer, embers/WUI → Built-Edge Reformer, fuel aridity → Climate-First, 98% initial attack → Suppression Modernizer, beneficial-fire gap → Cultural Fire Steward, aridity+embers → Thinning Skeptic), and every above-fold stat note carries its own key caveat (the 98% note carries the escaped-fire cost tail; the fire-deficit note carries the 'mostly dry, frequent-fire types' scope limit; the LA firestorm label frames it as a single event).

'Wildland-urban interface' (stat 3 label+note) is the one above-fold term whose definition lives only in the detail field; it is largely self-decoding, but a 3–4 word gloss in the note (e.g. 'where homes meet wild vegetation') would remove all doubt for a general reader.

Stat 7 (Acres burned 2024) note reads mildly self-contradictory in compact: 'both above the 10-year average, a season typical of the last decade.' Consider 'slightly above the 10-year average — a season typical of the last decade' to resolve the tension in one pass.

Crux subtitle: 'in the sky' is ambiguous — it most naturally reads as aircraft (Suppression Modernizer) but must mean the atmosphere (Climate-First) for the four/two mapping to work, since 'at first smoke' already covers suppression. The mapping still decodes against the six visible steelmen, so not blocking, but 'in the atmosphere' or 'in the emissions curve' would be unambiguous.

Beneficial-fire stat (stat 4): the fact that actual prescribed-fire acreage runs at roughly half the 400,000-acre goal is detail-only; the compact picture (goal ≈ 9% of the historic rate) is correct without it, so this is fine — just noting the strongest detail-only fact on the board.

Q4 (insurance/underwriting) is the only above-fold question whose anchor stat (FAIR Plan premiums) sits below the fold; the overview why_now ('insurers retreating from fire country') supplies compact grounding, so the question stands on its own.

The Cultural Fire Steward's central governance question (T4, burn authority) is below the fold, but the position's above-fold steelman ('give the authority to burn back...') carries the tension in compact, so the position is not hollowed out above the fold.

Compact/expanded split is working: every stat, question, and position 'detail' genuinely adds mechanism, precise figures, or methodology over its compact line — no restatement found. Compact jargon is consistently glossed in-tile ('fire deficit', 'defensible space', 'initial attack', 'FAIR Plan · state insurer of last resort', 'wildland-urban interface' spelled out).

Stat 2 unit 'M ha missing' uses the bare abbreviation 'ha' in the compact layer, and hectares in an otherwise acres-denominated topic; the note spells out 'hectares' so it parses, but rendering the unit as 'M hectares missing' would remove the stumble without touching the fact.

Stat 1 label 'Fuel aridity increase from warming · share attributable, since 1970s' is the most technical compact phrasing above the fold ('fuel aridity', 'share attributable'); the note immediately glosses it as 'fuel dryness', which keeps it at parity — a label like 'Fuel drying from warming' would hit the compact bar more cleanly if easy.

Action 2 description opens with bare 'IBHS's' at its point of use; the acronym is expanded in stat 5's source label but not here — a one-time gloss ('the insurance industry's research institute IBHS') would fix it.

Thinning Skeptic detail uses 'NEPA/ESA review' as bare acronyms without the define-at-first-use gloss the expanded register calls for — a two-word insert ('full environmental-review (NEPA/ESA)') suffices. Similarly, Climate-First detail spells out 'vapor pressure deficit' but never tags it '(VPD)' before switching to the acronym later in the paragraph.
Question details Q1 and Q2 carry several 50–80-word sentences; expanded register tolerates density but a tightening pass would improve scannability. Not a fit violation.

Built-Edge Reformer and Thinning Skeptic descriptions carry inline academic citations ('(Bradley, Hanson & DellaSala, Ecosphere 2016)', '(Zald & Dunn, Ecological Applications 2018)') — expanded-register citation density in the always-visible description layer, heavier than the sibling positions; the description field isn't in the strict compact list, so noted rather than flagged.

Basics T1 selection logic is strong: exactly one core stat per position (aridity→Climate-First, fire deficit→Landscape Restorer, WUI share→Built-Edge, beneficial-fire gap→Cultural Fire Steward, embers→Built-Edge/Skeptic, initial-attack 98%→Suppression debate), so the T1/T2 boundary sits at a genuine drop-off from argument-cores to context.

Weakest above-fold basic is 'Acres burned · US wildfires, 2024' — its own note calls the season 'typical of the last decade,' so it carries the least decision weight of the eight. If any swap is worth considering, it is with 'California FAIR Plan premiums,' which directly substantiates the why_now hook (insurer retreat) and the above-fold underwriting question. Not blocking: the LA-firestorm stat's note already surfaces insured losses ($25-30B) above the fold, and a topline annual-scale number has legitimate orientation value.

Questions fold (4/7) is well chosen: the master attribution question and the thinning-vs-skeptic question at T1, the suppression fire-debt tradeoff and who-pays at T2 — those four span all six positions' central disputes. The drop-off to Q5-Q7 (mechanism detail, let-burn, burn authority) is real.

Minor asymmetry: Cultural Fire Steward is a T1 position whose signature question (burn authority) is the sole T4, below fold. This tracks its prevalence weight (38) and its stat (beneficial-fire gap) is above the fold, so the camp is still represented; T4 vs T3 only affects ordering behind 'Go deeper,' not the fold itself.
Positions 6/6 above the fold in true prevalence order (85/72/60/55/38/22) is correct honest-non-balance presentation — hiding any camp behind the fold would have been the defect, and there is none.

prevalence_basis.name: Landscape Restorer
prevalence_basis.sketch: A century of fire exclusion loaded the land; thin, burn, and restore fire-adapted forests at scale.

prevalence_basis.name: Built-Edge Reformer
prevalence_basis.sketch: Losses happen where homes meet fuel — harden structures, rethink edge land use, and let insurance price the risk.

prevalence_basis.name: Climate-First Advocate
prevalence_basis.sketch: Fire weather is the driver; without cutting emissions, every acre treated and home hardened is triage.

prevalence_basis.name: Suppression Modernizer
prevalence_basis.sketch: Detect every start in minutes and hit it with overwhelming, round-the-clock force before it grows.

prevalence_basis.name: Cultural Fire Steward
prevalence_basis.sketch: These are fire-tended lands; return burning authority to the Indigenous stewards who kept them in balance.

prevalence_basis.name: Thinning Skeptic
prevalence_basis.sketch: Weather, not backcountry fuel, drives megafires; thinning is logging by another name — defend the home zone and let wildland fire work.
